title: i used claude code to help make a golf game that fits in 13 kilobytes
author: Slackluster
selftext:
Sunshine Golf Classic is an 18 hole 3D golf game that fits in 13KB. I have a ton of experience making small games like this but I wasn't sure if Claude would be good at size coding. I had to teach it a lot but we ended up being a really good team.

What made it work was giving it better ways to check itself. The build fails if the zip goes a byte over 13k. There are 226 headless tests and a bot plays a full round in the terminal and prints the score. So after any change we could see right away if the course got easier or harder.

That's most of the trick. It's good at building tools that measure things, and good at grinding through measurements I don't have the patience for.

I would sometimes send it to find bytes and it was almost never able to on its own. But if I had a specific idea of how to refactor or change something I could point it at that and it could make the changes and try it out.

At the end of the day I still hand wrote most of the code. I found most of the bytes myself because it didn't know where to look, and did all the gameplay and balance. But it was a good teammate for the parts that are just work. It was also helpful for talking through design changes and gameplay mechanics.

I'm sure claude and other ai agents will make a huge impact in this year's js13k contest. There is still about a week left if you want to try making something.

My game is submitted and you can play it on the official JS13k site...

[https://js13kgames.com/2026/games/sunshine-golf-classic#play](https://js13kgames.com/2026/games/sunshine-golf-classic#play)
